response.rationale: R3 is the unifying diagnosis: suppressed TSH, elevated free T4, and positive TSH-receptor antibody establish hyperthyroidism, which explains the atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and thromboembolic/thrombus burden. R2 is a strong acute complication with CT-proven pulmonary embolism and elevated D-dimer, but it is downstream of the thyroid disease. R5 is also downstream; R1/R6 are isolated valvular findings; C1-C4 are redundant restatements of parent candidates.

rejected.why: Severe mitral regurgitation is an isolated echocardiographic finding and does not explain the thyroid axis, atrial fibrillation, or pulmonary embolism.
Moderate mitral stenosis is an isolated echocardiographic finding and does not account for the hyperthyroid labs or thromboembolic complications.
Atrial fibrillation is a downstream complication of hyperthyroidism; ECG support is strong but it does not explain the thyroid labs, pulmonary embolism, or valvular/thrombotic findings.
Redundant append-only completion of R6; same raw span with a severity modifier, no independent diagnostic value.
Redundant append-only completion of R1; same raw span with a severity modifier, no independent diagnostic value.
Redundant append-only completion of R2; restates the CT pulmonary embolism finding with location/acuity modifiers, no independent diagnostic value.
Redundant append-only completion of R5; restates the atrial fibrillation rate, no independent diagnostic value.
